Torres del Paine in Patagonia: three granite spires rising sheer two-thousand meters from turquoise glacial lake, wind-scoured east faces dropping vertical, blue-grey ridges receding to horizon
Reynisfjara in Iceland: hexagonal basalt column cliffs rising sixty meters from north-Atlantic shore, charcoal-black volcanic sand beach stretching wide, sea-stacks standing fifty meters offshore
Namib Desert at Sossusvlei: thousand-foot rust-orange star dunes flanking bone-white cracked clay pan, shadow-striped ridgelines converging to vanishing point, apricot and deep-ochre sand walls
Vatnajökull Glacier in Iceland: ice cap stretching to horizon, electric-blue calving fronts dropping vertical into black volcanic-sand fjord, crevasse fields scoring the surface for kilometers
Grand Canyon in Arizona: one-mile-deep layered sandstone and limestone gorge, eighteen miles wide, rust-red and cream-white strata stepping down to the dark-schist inner gorge
Dolomites in northern Italy: sheer cream-white and rose-tinged limestone towers rising twelve-hundred meters from dark pine forest floor, vertical east faces split by deep couloirs
Nā Pali Coast on Kauai: fluted green basalt sea cliffs rising four-thousand feet directly from Pacific swells, narrow hanging valleys scoring the ridgelines, deep cobalt water below
Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia: twelve-thousand square kilometers of blinding white hexagonal salt crust at 3,656-meter elevation, mirror-flat to horizon, distant volcanic cones rising at the edge
Lemaire Channel in Antarctica: two-kilometer-wide passage flanked by vertical glaciated peaks rising nine-hundred meters, fractured blue-white ice floes covering the black polar water below
Bryce Canyon in Utah: amphitheater of thousands of rust-red and cream sandstone hoodoos dropping six-hundred feet from plateau rim, packed column forests filling the curved bowl
Cliffs of Moher in Ireland: vertical two-hundred-meter sea cliffs running fourteen kilometers along Atlantic coast, layered Liscannor flagstone in slate-grey and amber-ochre horizontal bands
Karakoram Highway corridor at K2 base: granite and gneiss faces of K2 rising 3,600 meters above the Baltoro Glacier, serrated black ridgelines, white glacial ice filling the valley floor
Wadi Rum in Jordan: sheer rose-red and amber sandstone massifs rising three-hundred meters from flat desert floor, narrow slot canyons cutting between, vast open plains of rust sand
Mount Bromo in East Java: active volcanic crater two-hundred meters deep inside a collapsed caldera ten kilometers wide, grey ash plain stretching to the outer caldera wall
Zhangjiajie in Hunan Province: over three-thousand sandstone pillars rising two-hundred to four-hundred meters vertically from valley floor, columns dressed in moss, deep ravines cutting between

Tre Cime di Lavaredo in the Italian Dolomites: three cylindrical dolomite towers rising nine-hundred meters sheer from a boulder-strewn plateau, north faces overhanging, pale-grey and cream rock splitting vertically
Étretat in Normandy: chalk-white sea cliffs rising ninety meters from grey-pebble beach, natural arches punching through the headlands, a freestanding chalk needle stack rising offshore

Banff Icefields Parkway in Alberta: Columbia Icefield spilling six square kilometers of blue-white glacial ice down between three-thousand-meter limestone peaks, moraines of pale rubble framing both flanks

Monument Valley on the Arizona-Utah border: six-hundred-meter rust-red Navajo sandstone buttes and mesas rising isolated from a flat desert plain, sheer vertical walls, talus skirts of deep-ochre debris
Fiordland at Milford Sound in New Zealand: granite and gneiss valley walls rising twelve-hundred meters sheer from dark fjord water, hanging valleys perched mid-cliff, mirror-smooth black water below

Atacama Desert at Valle de la Luna in Chile: cracked salt-flat basin flanked by jagged salt-and-gypsum ridges, terracotta and ash-white mineral crust, eroded clay formations rising ten meters from the pan

Kirkjufell Mountain on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula: steep-sided syenite peak rising four-hundred-sixty-three meters from sea level in a near-symmetrical cone, surrounded by grey lava field and cobalt fjord
Greenland Ice Sheet at Ilulissat Icefjord: calving glacier front four kilometers wide and eighty meters tall, fractured blue-white seracs collapsing into a fjord choked with car-sized ice debris
Zion Narrows in Utah: slot canyon one-thousand feet deep and twenty feet wide, rose-red and cream Navajo sandstone walls curving continuously, layered cross-bedding visible in every vertical face

Twelve Apostles on Victoria's Great Ocean Road: limestone sea stacks rising forty-five meters from Southern Ocean swells, amber and cream-layered rock faces, wave-cut platforms of pale stone at their bases

Cerro Torre in Patagonia: needle-thin granite and rime-encrusted tower rising three-thousand-one-hundred meters, vertical east face dropping sheer eight-hundred meters, flanked by glaciated col and lateral moraines
Hoh Rainforest in Olympic National Park: old-growth Sitka spruce and Douglas fir reaching sixty meters, every trunk and branch mantled in thick chartreuse moss, fern floor covering the entire valley

Jiuzhaigou Valley in Sichuan: travertine terraced lakes stacked in a glaciated limestone valley, electric turquoise and cobalt water over white calcite steps, submerged dead trunks visible through the clarity

Namib-Naukluft Tsauchab riverbed at Deadvlei: dead camel-thorn trees standing on a white clay pan enclosed by four-hundred-meter apricot-orange dunes, dune crests sharp-edged and sheer above the flat floor

Lofoten Islands in Norway: steep quartzite and granite peaks rising seven-hundred meters directly from the Norwegian Sea, narrow rock ridges connecting summits, dark cobalt water filling the fjords between
